403 discoveries announced in 2021

About AI discoveries in 2021

This selection contains 403 catalog entries dated 6 Jan 2021 to 31 Dec 2021. 403 include structured evidence annotations describing reported tests, the AI contribution and remaining limits. Missing annotations mean those details have not been structured here, not that a study lacks evidence.

Dates follow the catalog publication policy. Coverage is selected and incomplete; entries can overlap or describe several results. Counts do not measure independent discoveries, clinical benefit or worldwide research output. Read the selection and evidence policy or compare catalog coverage by year and field.

31 Dec 2021Research Center of Structural Health Monitoring and Prognosis

Fatigue Crack Evaluation with the Guided Wave-Convolutional Neural Network Ensemble and Differential Wavelet Spectrogram.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A guided-wave CNN ensemble estimated fatigue-crack length on a tested lap-joint specimen; on held-out specimen D6 the reported RMSE was 1.7 mm, with crack lengths followed during fatigue loading.

Technology: Differential time-frequency spectrograms from guided-wave signals were inputs to 20 CNNs; trained on specimens D1–D5, Methods §§2–3.

Editorial relevance 47 materials Published article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Differential time-frequency spectrograms from guided-wave signals were inputs to 20 CNNs; trained on specimens D1–D5, Methods §§2–3.
Test and result
Results §4 evaluates specimen D6 and reports agreement with measured crack lengths; maximum error 3 mm and RMSE 1.7 mm.
Limitation / still unknown
One held-out specimen, 77 training images and laboratory fatigue testing; authors note small training data and dependence on collected training data.

31 Dec 2021Aix-Marseille Université; Assistance Publique–Hôpitaux de Marseille; Laveran Military Teaching Hospital

Respiratory signals supported retrospective COVID-19 ICU risk stratification

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A Gaussian mixture model grouped respiratory-rate and oxygen-saturation signals from 279 ICU patients with COVID-19 to estimate intubation risk and a 24-hour severity score. The study reports 87.8% intubation recognition (AUC 0.94), three score-associated risk groups, and 81.0% accuracy for ICU stays over five days at a score threshold above 40. It is a retrospective single-setting result, not evidence of improved care or transportability.

Technology: Unsupervised Gaussian mixture model

Editorial relevance 47 medicine Published article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The unsupervised model clustered oxygen-saturation and respiratory-rate signals and derived hourly intubation probabilities summarized as a severity score.
Test and result
Retrospective data from one French ICU across two pandemic periods; outcomes were observed intubation and length of stay. No prospective clinical-impact evaluation is reported.
Limitation / still unknown
No independent, prospective or clinical-impact evaluation is reported unless specified in the tested field.

30 Dec 2021Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

Looking for low vision: Predicting visual prognosis by fusing structured and free-text data from electronic health records.

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Deep-learning models fused structured EHR data and ophthalmology notes to predict whether low vision would improve within a year; on 300 held-out patients, domain-specific text embeddings improved AUROC to about 0.82 versus structured-only and entity-based approaches. This is a bounded retrospective clinical prognosis result. Organization is unavailable in the deposited bibliographic metadata.

Technology: Deep-learning models combining EHR text and structured data

23 Dec 2021Chifeng Municipal Hospital; Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences; Genies (Beijing) Co., Ltd.

Histology and clinical features classify recorded HER2-positive recurrence in a separate cohort

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A ResNet50-based model combined histology features with clinical data to classify recorded recurrence or metastasis in HER2-positive breast cancer. Developed in 127 patients, it achieved a reported AUC of 0.72 in 123 TCGA patients. The result is retrospective clinical validation, without a time-calibrated recurrence forecast or demonstrated treatment benefit.

Technology: ResNet50; multimodal compact bilinear fusion

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned image features and multimodal fusion enable the source-specific classification of recorded recurrence outcomes.
Test and result
ResNet50 patch features were fused with clinical variables; patch scores were averaged per slide. Separate TCGA data supplied the represented AUC.
Limitation / still unknown
Internal two-fold splitting is described in terms of patches/samples without established patient separation. Follow-up horizons and censoring are not adequately specified for a time-calibrated prognosis. Histology heterogeneity and different cohort characteristics limit reproducibility. No prospective validation, avoided treatment or improved clinical outcomes were measured.

30 Nov 2021Lehigh University; University of Maryland; University of Pennsylvania; Georgia State University; Georgia Institute of Technology; Emory University

Graph-selected brain connectivity is associated with ADHD symptom scores

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A dynamic graph convolutional network analyzed resting-state scans from 603 ADHD-200 participants. Model-selected connectivity features were associated with symptom severity in a 172-person subgroup. These retrospective, post-selection associations are exploratory and do not establish a causal ADHD mechanism or clinical utility.

Technology: Dynamic graph convolutional network (dGCN) and isolation forest

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned graph convolutions ranked regional connectivity features used to investigate symptom associations; a separate conventional linear regression quantified symptom-score prediction. The claimed result is the exploratory AI-selected association, not a causal mechanism.
Test and result
The selected four-site sample contained 260 ADHD and 343 control participants after isolation-forest outlier removal. dGCN combined connectivity with seven personal-characteristic variables and reached 72.0% diagnostic accuracy in site-stratified ten-fold cross-validation; leave-site-out accuracy ranged from 67.9% to 74.3%. Across 172 Peking University participants with symptom scales, regression on model-selected regional features yielded cross-validated symptom-score correlations of .33–.36. Selected within-frontal, within-posterior-fossa and subcortical–posterior-fossa connectivity showed symptom correlations of .28–.34, reported with FDR correction.
Limitation / still unknown
Regional selection used model weights averaged across diagnostic cross-validation. Its independence from the subsequent symptom regression and correlation analyses is not established; FDR correction does not remove selection bias. All symptom analyses used a subset of the same source dataset. Imaging alone did not supply the reported diagnostic predictions: age, sex, handedness and IQ-related inputs were included. Site-held-out classification is not independent replication of the selected biological associations. No causal direction, independent symptom-cohort confirmation or benefit from clinical use is established. The November2021 online version is represented; the issue date is February2022, and the bounded search does not establish earliest public priority.

Voice classifiers distinguish COVID groups in a small held-out sample

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A study trained voice classifiers in 210 participants and tested their combined predictions in 30 additional participants. The system classified 24 of 30 correctly, including all 10 positive cases. The selected symptomatic, Italian-speaking sample does not establish asymptomatic screening performance or population-level accuracy.

Technology: Radial-basis support vector machines on acoustic features

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
SVMs learned acoustic distinctions between clinically defined groups from extracted voice features; voting combined task-specific predictions.
Test and result
Three cohorts of 70 participants supplied voice recordings for feature selection and binary SVM training. Separately recruited test participants comprised 10 positive,10 recovered and 10 healthy individuals. Table 5 reports 24/30 correct,10/10 positive,8/10 healthy and 6/10 recovered. Majority voting combined three tasks and three binary comparisons.
Limitation / still unknown
Training feature selection/ranking precedes the described ten-fold evaluation, so internal cross-validation is not clearly nested; repeated recordings also need participant-level separation. The 30-person test is a small balanced within-study sample, not independent replication. Table 5 includes one uncertain recovered participant, despite an abstract statement that all errors were classified positive. Most positive/recovered patients were symptomatic, and language/ethnicity restrictions constrain generalization. Long-term vocal effects and surveillance benefit were not demonstrated.

Digital kidney-biopsy damage features are associated with later graft loss

Technology: Mask R-CNN and U-Net histopathology analysis

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Neural tissue/immune-cell segmentation supplied quantitative damage features, which ordinary survival analysis related to subsequent graft outcomes.
Test and result
Networks were developed on 60 selected biopsy slides and tested on 33 others. The pipeline then analyzed 478 baseline and 311 twelve-month slides from 404 GoCAR and 212 AUSCAD participants. In 200 GoCAR and 111 AUSCAD twelve-month biopsies, composite tissue/inflammation scores were associated with later death-censored graft loss; thresholds were derived in GoCAR.
Limitation / still unknown
This is retrospective image/outcome analysis of previously collected cohorts, not prospective evaluation of a frozen clinical tool. GoCAR supplies both selected model-development slides and outcome analyses, with exact patient overlap not separated here. Baseline ITAS survival association was not confirmed in AUSCAD. Observational associations, selected thresholds, limited graft-loss events and cohort differences prevent causal, treatment-benefit or universal surrogate-endpoint claims.

9 Oct 2021Zwicky Transient Facility collaboration; California Institute of Technology; Liverpool John Moores University; University of California, Berkeley; collaborating observatories

Real-time discovery and characterization of AT2020xnd, an AT2018cow-like fast transient

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: ZTF observations identified AT2020xnd (ZTF20acigmel) at redshift 0.243 as the first unambiguous AT2018cow analogue found and confirmed in real time. Follow-up showed a rapid optical rise, persistently hot blue emission, luminous radio, millimetre and X-ray output, no classical radioactive-supernova peak, and a dwarf-galaxy host. The authors argue that these properties support a distinct fast-blue-optical-transient phenomenon, while its progenitor and central engine remain uncertain.

Technology: Zwicky Transient Facility real-time alert stream with a deep-learning real-bogus classifier and a custom contextual transient filter

Editorial relevance 53 astronomy Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The paper’s custom search filter required the ZTF alert’s deep-learning real-bogus score to exceed 0.65, along with repeated detections, a high Galactic latitude and no coincident stellar counterpart. This AI-based alert filtering contributed to selecting AT2020xnd in real time; rapid multiband photometry and spectroscopic and multiwavelength human follow-up established its astrophysical nature and unusual properties.
Test and result
ZTF observations identified AT2020xnd (ZTF20acigmel) at redshift 0.243 as the first unambiguous AT2018cow analogue found and confirmed in real time.
Limitation / still unknown
This is one transient and a small class comparison, not a general population measurement. The AI contribution was alert filtering, not autonomous physical interpretation or confirmation; telescope follow-up was essential. The suggested distinct phenomenon is supported by shared observed properties, while the progenitor/engine interpretation remains unresolved and model-dependent.

Editorial relevance 33 biology Published article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned networks detected and classified suspicious regions from patient MRI; comparison with expert labels and available biopsy outcomes produced the represented diagnostic-validation result. Low performance is retained rather than treated as evidence of clinical utility.
Test and result
The source reports 150 held-out scans with 198 expert-marked lesions. After benign-hyperplasia filtering, the algorithm detected 111 of 198 lesions, with PPV 62.7% and overall PI-RADS accuracy 30.8%. Among 136 lesions with targeted biopsy, 82.3% of detected reference lesions were tumor-positive, while 50.9% of missed reference lesions were benign. This is a specific clinical evaluation with partial pathology follow-up, beyond a public image benchmark alone.
Limitation / still unknown
Detection/reference categories were defined by one expert radiologist rather than complete histopathology. False-positive regions lacked targeted-biopsy validation, preventing full cancer detection-rate assessment. Cohort totals are supported by Figure 1, but abstract/Methods split counts conflict; pathology-grade subtotals also do not fully reconcile. Prostate-X includes repeated scans, and individual-patient separation across all partitions was not reconstructed. No reader-assistance benefit, prospective workflow evaluation or clinical efficacy was demonstrated.

AI contribution

Test and result
The study included 38 chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy cases, 17 rheumatic heart disease cases and 12 healthy controls. An 80:20 random split was described for LASSO logistic classification; the selected panel comprised IL-12p70, IL-7, IL-1Ra and IL-4.

No pathogen experimentation or therapeutic intervention is represented.

23 Sep 2021Emory University; Council for Scientific and Industrial Research; North-West University; University of Pretoria

Random forests map South African particulate pollution patterns

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A random-forest analysis combined ground stations, satellite data and environmental predictors to estimate daily particulate pollution around Gauteng during 2014–2018. It mapped persistent hotspots and seasonal differences, with lower estimated concentrations in much of the region after 2016. The comparison does not establish a policy effect.

Technology: Random forest exposure regression

Editorial relevance 33 climate Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned tree ensembles infer particulate concentrations from satellite, meteorological, land-use and socioeconomic inputs; the field result is the resulting bounded regional exposure pattern.
Test and result
The model used 9,853 station-day observations from 20 monitors and 40 predictors. Random ten-fold cross-validation gave R² .80 and RMSE 9.40 µg/m³. Predicted winter concentrations were highest; Johannesburg and surrounding areas showed little clear change between 2014–2015 and 2016–2018 while much of the domain decreased.
Limitation / still unknown
Station-day random folds do not demonstrate transfer to unseen monitoring sites or future years. The model underestimates very high concentrations; top-quintile CV R² was .69. Satellite missingness and correction introduce additional uncertainty. A before/after-policy indicator is itself a model predictor, and the comparison has no causal control or counterfactual. Maps are modeled estimates, not complete ground measurements. No individual health benefit is measured.

AI contribution
The authors built neural-network potentials from first-principles data, screened 396,862 PtFeCu nanoparticle configurations, and used the predicted ternary configuration/composition map to guide experimental synthesis and selection of catalyst variants. Editorial relevance 53 physics Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The authors’ AI-enabled automated design algorithm used an interpretable weighted, colored-graph representation of photonic experiments, gradient-based optimization, and topology reduction to search open experiment-design problems and expose generalizable physical concepts. The authors identify the work as explainable AI; the contribution is the algorithmically found design/concept, not merely faster benchmarking.
Test and result
The interpretable THESEUS design algorithm produced a three-dimensional six-photon GHZ-state blueprint that suppresses unwanted state terms toward arbitrarily high fidelity, with lower count rates, and a heralded three-dimensional Bell-state blueprint using destructive interference to cancel vacuum contributions.
Limitation / still unknown
These are theoretically calculated experiment blueprints, not experimentally demonstrated states in this paper. For the six-photon GHZ design, unwanted amplitudes can be reduced arbitrarily by adjusting graph weights, at the cost of lower count rates; feasibility is argued for contemporary photonics. The heralded Bell design’s estimated count rate and fidelity are modeled, not measured.

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned MRI-to-CT synthesis supplied images for a defined dosimetric reference comparison; conventional treatment-planning software computed the plans.
Test and result
The 37 patients supplied 2,561 liver-region image slices. Ten-fold evaluation grouped patients, leaving 3–4 people out per fold. Synthetic images generated for held-out cases were compared with each patient’s original CT in target/organ-at-risk planning. Perceptual and MSE variants had mean absolute image errors of 35.64 and 35.67 HU, and all synthetic-CT plans met the source planning objectives.
Limitation / still unknown
The same small single-system cohort informed preliminary training choices, so this is not an external independent validation. Missing fine structures such as ribs and registration between separately acquired MRI/CT remain limitations. Reported nonsignificant comparisons are not equivalence tests, and visual image quality is not delivered-dose safety. Manual target contours were transferred from original CT; an entirely CT-free clinical workflow was not tested. No actual treatment-outcome comparison or demonstrated clinical benefit is reported. The August 2021 online version is represented; its issue date is 2022.

Cell-free DNA fragmentomes distinguish lung cancer in two clinical cohorts

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A LASSO-regularized classifier using genome-wide cell-free DNA fragmentation distinguished lung cancer in a prospectively collected 365-person clinical cohort, with cross-validated AUC 0.90. A fixed model was evaluated in an independent group of 385 non-cancer individuals and 46 lung-cancer patients, while a separate multimodal model was evaluated only within the original cohort. These results establish a diagnostic proof of concept, not screening benefit: a 2022 commentary questioned extrapolation from mostly symptomatic patients, and the authors agreed that screening-cohort development and validation were still needed.

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Published article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
PCA is fitted within training folds, and LASSO-regularized logistic regression learns a cancer-risk score from fragmentome and chromosomal-arm features. A fixed learned model then predicts cancer status in an independent cohort.
Test and result
Among 365 analyzed LUCAS participants, model training/evaluation used 158 without prior/baseline/future cancer and 129 with baseline lung cancer. PCA within training folds compressed fragment-size features; LASSO logistic regression included chromosomal-arm measures, with repeated fivefold cross-validation. A final model and cutoffs were applied to 385 non-cancer individuals and 46 predominantly early-stage lung-cancer patients from separate collections. The main-cohort AUC was 0.90 (95% CI 0.86–0.94).
Limitation / still unknown
Most LUCAS participants were symptomatic and all had suspicious imaging; prospective collection does not establish prospective evaluation of a frozen model. The combined fragment/clinical/CEA model was not evaluated in the external cohort. A 2022 commentary challenged screening extrapolation, and the authors described the work as proof of concept needing screening-population validation; clinical benefit, sensitivity to very small lesions and safety of pre-CT triage were not established.

The model generated seed cell-penetrating sequences, predicted quantitative nuclear-delivery activity from peptide fingerprints, and iteratively optimized sequences for higher predicted activity subject to length, charge, similarity and solubility constraints. Safety evidence is limited to reported assays/doses and short follow-up.

28 Jul 2021Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center

Learned muscle segmentation adds constraints to head-and-neck radiotherapy replanning

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: In a retrospective ten-patient planning study, learned organ segmentations enabled additional masticatory-muscle constraints in an automated optimizer. All replanned cases then satisfied the selected muscle-dose criteria. This was a computational plan comparison using previously developed cases, not evidence of reduced trismus in treated patients.

Technology: UnetSA and DeepLabV3+ with ResNet-101 organ segmentation

Editorial relevance 33 medicine Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Previously trained segmentation networks supplied organ/muscle masks that reduced the annotation burden for adding structures. ECHO optimization and dose calculation were conventional components, not silently attributed to learned AI.
Test and result
Each of 10 cases was replanned with the conventional ECHO optimizer under manual masks, learned replacement masks, and learned masks plus additional muscle constraints. The latter configuration met both selected muscle criteria for all cases, correcting one remaining violation in the other configurations. Comparisons used the 20-Gy boost phase, with criteria scaled from the full prescription; these units explain the differing table/abstract dose values.
Limitation / still unknown
These ten cases had previously been used to develop the planning pipeline and are not a fresh independent validation cohort. The trismus criteria came from an earlier observational risk model; no prospective patient follow-up or reduction in actual trismus was measured. Learned masks and manually defined masks differed geometrically, so nominal plan dose changes are not directly established improvements in delivered anatomy. The additional constraints did not yield statistically significant overall organ-dose differences in the compared scenarios. Existing clinical ECHO use for other cancer sites does not validate this head-and-neck application.

5 Jul 2021University of Pennsylvania

Simulated low-field MRI retains pathology-detection signals with reduced small-lesion sensitivity

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: First posted in July 2021 and journal-published that December, this study used DenseNet-121 classifiers to compare pathology detection in 3T MRI and simulated 64mT-quality images from glioma, stroke and multiple-sclerosis datasets. Patient-separated tests reported similar slice-level AUCs, including 0.97 versus 0.98 for low-grade glioma, while simulated low-field sensitivity declined for smaller lesions. The transformation had limited paired-image and radiologist checks, but omitted field-dependent tissue contrast and device artifacts; these simulations do not establish diagnostic equivalence or clinical performance of an actual low-field scanner.

Technology: DenseNet-121 convolutional neural network for pathology detection

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
DenseNet-121, initialized with ImageNet weights, learns lesion-present versus lesion-absent image classification. Comparing held-out original and simulated datasets probes a specific imaging-performance question; the image transformation itself was conventional rather than learned.
Test and result
A non-neural image transformation was fitted using three hydrocephalus patients and checked in three additional patients; three radiologists compared paired real/simulated images from ten MS patients. DenseNet-121 classifiers were trained separately on original/simulated images for low-grade glioma (76 subjects), high-grade glioma (259), stroke (28) and MS (20), using approximately 9:1 patient-separated train/test splits. Reported slice-level AUCs were respectively 0.97/0.98, 0.96/0.95, 0.94/0.94 and 0.90/0.87.
Limitation / still unknown
The simulation approximates resolution/noise but not all field-strength contrast or device-specific artifacts. Separate disease classifiers perform simple lesion detection, not differential diagnosis or full radiologic assessment. Small test cohorts and degraded detection of small lesions limit generalization; prospective actual-device trials and patient benefit were not established.

AI contribution
The detector CNN scanned continuous raw three-component waveform windows for earthquake signals; a second CNN classified distance and magnitude, enabling the researchers to find and characterize uncataloged events from a single station. The CNN pipeline generated the new event detections; authors then visually checked them.
Test and result
A two-stage 1D CNN pipeline applied to continuous three-component seismic waveforms from one L’Aquila station identified 273 previously uncataloged local earthquake events during a one-month 2009 foreshock period.
Limitation / still unknown
The analysis covers one month in February 2009 from one station. The authors report 273 new local detections and six nonlocal events among 369 windows classified as local; all 273 new detections were visually confirmed. The pipeline does not provide exact event locations, and transfer to other regions was not established. Magnitudes are coarse classes, not precise estimates.

iTARGEX analysis identifies ELG1 as a regulator of yeast transcription buffering and four protein-turnover regulators

Experiments supported ELG1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of transcriptional buffering during S phase; the phenotype was reproduced in a second genetic background and rescued by a PCNA-D150E mutation. Follow-up protein-turnover measurements showed altered turnover in MRN1, UPF3, RAM1 and SSN3 deletion strains.

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
iTARGEX associated gene-expression profiles from deletion strains with biological traits without requiring prior gene annotations and nominated candidate regulators. The researchers then performed S-phase transcription and protein-turnover experiments to test the model-prioritized candidates, supporting ELG1's role in transcriptional buffering and altered turnover for four deletion strains.
Test and result
Experiments supported ELG1 as a previously unrecognized regulator of transcriptional buffering during S phase; the phenotype was reproduced in a second genetic background and rescued by a PCNA-D150E mutation.
Limitation / still unknown
The study used budding yeast and pre-existing deletion-mutant transcriptome profiles, followed by experiments on selected candidates. ELG1's role in S-phase transcription buffering was reproduced in a second yeast genetic background and rescued by PCNA-D150E; the protein-turnover effects concern yeast deletion strains. These results do not establish corresponding human functions.

27 Jun 2021ETH Zurich; Thomas Jefferson University; University of Bari; University of Innsbruck; Goethe University Frankfurt; Friedrich Schiller University Jena

Machine-intelligence design yields selective synthetic COX-1 inhibitors from a marine natural-product template

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Using Marinopyrrole A as a template, an automated design workflow generated and synthesized new natural-product-inspired molecules; target-prediction software pointed to cyclooxygenases. In biochemical assays, synthetic mimetics 2 and 2a inhibited COX-1 at 0.10 and 0.16 μM, respectively, and compound 2a was crystallographically observed bound to COX-1. Human platelet assays also showed inhibition.

Technology: DOGS rule-based de novo molecule construction and CATS molecular-similarity ranking, coupled with SPiDER self-organizing-map machine-learning target prediction

Editorial relevance 60 chemistry Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
DOGS algorithmically generated natural-product-inspired structures and suggested synthetic routes; CATS ranked candidates by pharmacophore similarity. SPiDER's cascaded self-organizing-map models predicted molecular target families, including COX. Experimental target assays confirmed the previously unrecognized COX-1 activity of selected synthetic compounds, with crystallographic confirmation for compound 2a.
Test and result
In biochemical assays, synthetic mimetics 2 and 2a inhibited COX-1 at 0.10 and 0.16 μM, respectively, and compound 2a was crystallographically observed bound to COX-1.
Limitation / still unknown
The study tests a small number of designed molecules; automated structure generation was rule-based and similarity-driven rather than a trained generative neural model. The COX-1 effects were biochemical/platelet assays, not clinical effects; the platelet IC50s for 2, 2a, 2b were 9, 13 and 56 nM, but COX-2 inhibition occurred at higher concentrations and selectivity varies by assay. Do not call these approved drugs or imply therapeutic benefit.

26 Jun 2021University of Sheffield; Imperial College London

Consensus learning nominates a pulmonary-hypertension miRNA pattern

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Four fitted feature-selection approaches consistently selected miR-636 and miR-187-5p in a pulmonary arterial hypertension study. The clinical miRNA models showed moderate discrimination in a small held-out subset. These are exploratory diagnostic-reference and feature-association findings, not established clinical utility or causal pulmonary mechanisms.

Technology: Boruta random forest; LASSO; regression partition trees; XGBoost

Editorial relevance 40 medicine Published article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned forests, boosted trees and regularized/partition models select diagnostic features and produce patient-level predictions; agreement of selected features and held-out reference discrimination supply the scoped finding.
Test and result
The miRNA cohort comprised 64 PAH cases and 43 combined healthy/systemic-sclerosis-without-PH controls. Models were developed using 72 people and assessed on 35; repeated cross-validation supported feature selection and tuning. Both nominated miRNAs recurred across the four approaches and alternative selection analyses.
Limitation / still unknown
Model and feature comparisons used the same small validation sample. The Results claim 30/35 correct for Boruta, while the table reports a different classification rate; no single accuracy is promoted here. Whole-data filtering and multiple selection analyses require caution. Whole-blood gene-target classification involved refitting on different features and is not external validation of the original miRNA classifier. A five-year follow-up does not make the already-collected diagnostic evaluation prospective. No pathway causality or laboratory mechanism is adopted.

17 Jun 2021Pennsylvania State University; Syracuse University

Machine-learning unmixing links acid rain and subsurface flowpaths to watershed CO₂ drawdown

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was applied to stream-chemistry time series from three watersheds to infer solute endmembers and their changing contributions without predefining endmember chemistry. Combined with geological interpretation and independent geochemical evidence, the model separated shallow acid-rain-affected flow from deeper pyrite-weathering contributions. The analysis found that acid rain can reduce a watershed’s long-timescale CO₂-sequestration capacity and that omitting sulfide oxidation/acid-rain reactions overestimates weathering-driven CO₂ drawdown.

Technology: Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) machine-learning blind-source-separation model applied to stream chemistry

Editorial relevance 53 climate Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The NMF model simultaneously inferred endmember chemical signatures and per-sample mixing proportions from solute ratios without preset endmember compositions. Researchers interpreted those patterns using watershed geology, sulfur isotopes, weathering profiles and calcite saturation, then estimated mineral-weathering rates and CO₂ sequestration. The ML decomposition enabled source separation where conventional endmember assumptions were uncertain; it did not directly measure a global carbon flux.
Test and result
Non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) was applied to stream-chemistry time series from three watersheds to infer solute endmembers and their changing contributions without predefining endmember chemistry.
Limitation / still unknown
This is an inference from historical stream chemistry and watershed-specific geology, not a direct measurement of global CO₂ sequestration or a causal intervention. The NMF endmembers were interpreted as subsurface flowpaths using geological knowledge and supporting geochemical evidence; the inferred acid-rain sulfate export at Shale Hills includes a 19–31-year lag estimate. The result applies to three studied watersheds and the weathering timescales considered. Endmember counts and interpretations depend on the model setup and watershed reaction-front assumptions.

This analysis exposed the model’s aerosol-sensitive regional signal and the higher year-prediction correlation of the network trained with aerosols held at 1920 levels.
Test and result
Using explainable AI on single-forcing CESM1 large ensembles, the study identified the North Atlantic, Southern Ocean and Southeast Asia as key regional temperature patterns for dating the climate simulations, particularly before the early 21st century.
Limitation / still unknown
This is a model-based attribution analysis from one climate model (CESM1) and historical/RCP8.5 simulations, with reanalysis used for evaluation; it is not a direct experiment or causal attribution of every observed regional trend. The relevance maps identify patterns useful to the trained network and do not by themselves prove a physical mechanism. The authors discuss other forcings, feedbacks and internal variability, and the net influence of aerosols remains uncertain.

Learned OCT texture analysis distinguishes sampled brain-metastasis tissue from healthy tissue

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A support-vector classifier separated OCT images of sampled brain metastases and healthy brain tissue using histology-derived labels. The analysis retained fourteen tissue samples from a twenty-patient collection. Reported image-level accuracy is exploratory: cross-validation split B-scans, without demonstrated separation of tissue samples or patients, and does not establish surgical diagnostic performance.

Technology: Support-vector machines on OCT texture features with PCA dimensionality reduction

Editorial relevance 33 biology Published article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The SVM combined learned boundaries over multifeature OCT texture measurements to discriminate histology-labeled sampled tissue categories, supplying a specific ex-vivo diagnostic feasibility result. PCA alone is not treated as the enabling AI contribution.
Test and result
Twenty patients contributed twenty-two tissue samples; histologic purity criteria retained ten tumor and four healthy samples. An experienced neuropathologist assigned tissue-composition reference labels. Texture features from 14,336 OCT B-scans were reduced with PCA and classified using grid-tuned SVMs with tenfold cross-validation. The source reports up to 96.83% image-level discrimination of pooled vital/necrotic tumor versus healthy tissue.
Limitation / still unknown
B-scans from the same tissue specimen are correlated, and the described allocation does not establish specimen-level or patient-level separation between folds. Normalization/PCA isolation and nested tuning are not established. Purity-selected specimens and small sample counts constrain interpretation; thousands of images do not substitute for independent patients. No intraoperative clinical deployment, margin-level ground truth, recurrence reduction or survival benefit was demonstrated.

26 Apr 2021Politecnico di Torino; National Research Council of Italy; Perugia Hospital; Terni Hospital

Urine-output neural model shows retrospective discrimination of severe kidney-injury events

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A convolutional neural network analyzed urine-output trends in 35,573 ICU patients to estimate later severe kidney-injury events under a restrictive urine-plus-creatinine definition. Patient-separated retrospective testing reported AUC 0.89, above logistic regression. Clinical prevention, calibrated alarm yield and prospective bedside benefit were not established.

Technology: Stacked and parallel convolutional neural networks with highway connections for urine-output time series

Editorial relevance 40 biology Published article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The CNN learned temporal urine-output features linked to later recorded severe-AKI labels and was compared with a logistic baseline. The admitted result is specific retrospective clinical discrimination, not recovery of a single urine-output cutoff or a validated intervention.
Test and result
The source pooled eICU and MIMIC-III records and separated patients across training, validation, calibration and test sets. The CNN used twelve-hour urine-output windows, with case series truncated six hours before the defined event. In the 7,080-patient test cohort, reported AUC was 0.89 versus 0.85 for logistic regression. The target required both creatinine increase and urine-output reduction; dialysis patients were excluded.
Limitation / still unknown
This was retrospective pooled-database evaluation, not a locked prospective clinical test. Urine output contributes to both model input and event definition; imputation and restrictive exclusions limit generalization to broader AKI. Reported likelihood ratios must not be read as positive predictive value or five true cases per six alarms. Individual-record timing, exact alarm yield and calibrated probabilities were not independently reconstructed. No reduced kidney injury, mortality or treatment benefit was demonstrated.

12 Apr 2021Ghent University; VIB Center for Plant Systems Biology; Bioinformatics Institute Ghent

An integrated Arabidopsis regulatory network predicts 13 previously unlinked reactive-oxygen-stress regulators

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Researchers integrated DNA-motif, chromatin-accessibility, TF-binding and expression evidence with supervised learning to build an Arabidopsis gene-regulatory network of 1,491 transcription factors and 1.7 million TF–target interactions. The network predicted candidate reactive-oxygen-species (ROS) regulators; loss- and gain-of-function phenotyping supported 13 regulators not previously linked to ROS or stress responses. Newly tested examples included WRKY55, WRKY47, AT2G33710 and AT5G57150. The paper also reports that 75% of its ROS-predicted TFs had ROS or physiological stress functions supported by either this study or prior evidence.

Technology: Supervised-learning integrated gene-regulatory network (iGRN) built from motif, open-chromatin, transcription-factor-binding and expression-based networks

Editorial relevance 60 biology Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The supervised integration model inferred TF–target regulatory links across multiple experimental input networks and predicted candidate TF functions, including ROS-response regulators. The investigators tested predicted TF candidates using Arabidopsis loss- or gain-of-function lines and ROS-specific phenotyping; these experiments supported 13 TFs without prior ROS/stress associations.
Test and result
Newly tested examples included WRKY55, WRKY47, AT2G33710 and AT5G57150.
Limitation / still unknown
The iGRN integrated existing experimental data and the ROS findings were tested in Arabidopsis stress assays, not crop-yield or field-resilience trials. The 75% figure combines prior literature with new phenotypic tests; it is not a rate of independently replicated new discoveries. The new TF functions are limited to tested oxidative-stress conditions and mutant lines.

19 Mar 2021NEC Corporation; National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST); Tohoku University; University of Tokyo; Japan Atomic Energy Agency

Autonomous ML search and experiments find Fe–Co–Ir/Pt alloys above the Slater–Pauling magnetization limit

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: A game-tree search using Gaussian-process predictions and first-principles calculations proposed dilute Ir and Pt additions as a counterintuitive way to raise Fe–Co magnetization. Combinatorial sputtering and magnetic measurements experimentally found Fe–Co–Ir and Fe–Co–Pt compositions with magnetization exceeding the conventional Fe₃Co₁ Slater–Pauling limit; the highest-moment points reported in the ternary maps were near Fe₈₁Co₁₅Ir₄ and Fe₈₅Co₁₁Pt₄. The study’s calculations attribute the effect to Ir/Pt-induced increases in local Fe and Co moments.

Technology: Autonomous materials search using a Gaussian-process regression model with game-tree search and an upper-confidence-bound acquisition rule, coupled to KKR-CPA first-principles calculations

Editorial relevance 60 materials Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
The autonomous system iteratively selected compositions in an eight-component disordered-alloy search using ab-initio magnetic-moment estimates and a game-tree Gaussian-process model balancing exploration and exploitation. After about 43 days it proposed Fe₈₂Co₁₃Ir₄Pt₁; that hypothesis directed combinatorial synthesis and testing of Fe–Co–Ir and Fe–Co–Pt spreads. The follow-up measurements found compositions surpassing the prior Fe₃Co₁ benchmark and motivated theoretical analysis of impurity-enhanced Fe/Co local moments.
Test and result
A game-tree search using Gaussian-process predictions and first-principles calculations proposed dilute Ir and Pt additions as a counterintuitive way to raise Fe–Co magnetization.
Limitation / still unknown
The highest-moment composition suggested by the autonomous search (Fe₈₂Co₁₃Ir₄Pt₁) was not itself the maximum in the measured ternary composition spreads; the Fe–Co–Ir and Fe–Co–Pt maps identified different peak compositions. The finding is based on sputtered, annealed thin-film composition spreads and room-temperature MOKE/SQUID measurements, not bulk ingots or device testing. The eight-element search space was narrowed by preliminary calculations. KKR-CPA results assume ideal disordered bulk states at 0 K, unlike the film measurements.

The source cohort contained 30 COVID-19 patients and 30 controls, contributing 705 and 990 CT slices respectively. 22 Jan 2021Georgia Institute of Technology

Transformer-classified reviews map regional patterns in EV availability discussions

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: BERT and XLNet classified topics in an archive of 127,257 U.S. charging-station reviews. Spatial analysis placed relatively frequent availability discussions in smaller communities in parts of the West and Midwest, with different patterns in the South and Northeast. The result concerns review-topic frequency, not independently measured charging shortages.

Technology: BERT and XLNet supervised topic classification

Editorial relevance 33 humanities Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Learned language classifiers scaled manual topic labels across the review corpus, enabling the source-specific spatial analysis. Conventional mapping summarized those learned labels; predicted discussion is kept distinct from observed infrastructure conditions.
Test and result
The 2011–2015 archive covered 12,720 charging locations and 29,532 users. Human-designed topics were learned from expert-annotated reviews; ten cross-validation runs gave overall accuracy 91.6% and F1 .83/.84 for BERT/XLNet. Predicted topic frequencies were mapped using 2013 metropolitan/micropolitan boundaries and standardized separately into regional quantiles. The source describes smaller-community availability discussion patterns in parts of the West/Midwest and more major-metropolitan patterns in the South/Northeast.
Limitation / still unknown
Availability is a broad discussion topic encompassing whether stations are available; frequent discussion is not a direct estimate of shortage, station failure or unmet demand. Regional quantile normalization prevents treating the map as a common absolute availability scale. Reviews appear only when users post, do not contain charging transactions and cannot establish population-wide access or causal infrastructure effects. The data were reanalyzed from an existing archive, and topics were manually specified rather than discovered unsupervised. Annotator experts were trained students, not industry professionals; the 100-review audited comparison does not establish universal superhuman annotation. Full supplemental training partitions and spatial counts were not reviewed, so geographic unit-count claims are not reproduced. This represents the January 2021 journal version, despite the 2020 DOI token.

ECG/VCG machine learning detected prevalent cardiovascular disease in the Jackson Heart Study cohort; the modest result is limited to cross-sectional risk detection.
Limitation / still unknown
The reviewed study does not establish validation or benefit beyond its reported evaluation.

19 Jan 2021Janelia Research Campus, Howard Hughes Medical Institute; National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, NIH

AI-photoswitchable CRISPRi screening identifies new regulators of TFEB localization during starvation

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: An image-classification-guided pooled CRISPRi screen mapped factors that affect TFEB movement from nucleus to cytosol during prolonged starvation. The screen identified multiple candidate genes, and follow-up assays independently validated 21 of 64 neural-network-called hits; experiments on CREB5 further linked it to TFEB retention and starvation-associated autophagy/lysosomal protein expression.

Technology: AI-photoswitchable screening (AI-PS), using SVM classifiers and a convolutional neural network

Editorial relevance 60 biology Published articlePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: direct test. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
SVM and CNN models classified single-cell images by subcellular protein localization; the system photoactivated cells with the target phenotype for FACS isolation and gRNA sequencing in pooled CRISPRi screening. AI enabled the genome-scale genotype-to-subcellular-phenotype screen.
Test and result
The screen identified multiple candidate genes, and follow-up assays independently validated 21 of 64 neural-network-called hits; experiments on CREB5 further linked it to TFEB retention and starvation-associated autophagy/lysosomal protein expression.
Limitation / still unknown
Only 21 of 64 neural-network-called TFEB hits were independently validated in secondary assays (about 32%); candidate effectors should not be treated as all confirmed. Results use cultured U2OS cells and prolonged starvation, and do not establish a physiological role in an organism. CREB5 received targeted follow-up but the overall screen has a modest validation rate.

14 Jan 2021MIT

Language models identify viral regions less prone to immune escape

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Analysis of influenza, HIV, and coronavirus sequences identifies regions of surface proteins less likely to mutate to escape immune responses, including the S2 subunit of spike. These are computational leads for studying possible vaccine targets, not validated vaccines.

Technology: Protein-sequence language model

Editorial relevance 60 biology Press releasePublished article Suggest a correction

Publication: Peer-reviewed paper · Test context: retrospective or benchmark. Catalog categories, not an evidence grade.

AI contribution
Adapted language-model methods to viral protein sequences to predict surface regions more or less likely to enable immune escape, as candidate vaccine targets.
Test and result
Language models trained on about 60,000 HIV, 45,000 influenza and 4,000 coronavirus sequences were checked against earlier findings on influenza and HIV; the SARS-CoV-2 analysis is described as not yet peer-reviewed.
Limitation / still unknown
Flagged SARS-CoV-2 sequences still need investigation, and it is unknown how fast SARS-CoV-2 mutates, so how long current vaccines stay effective is unclear.

Bayesian models prioritize compounds for Schistosoma mansoni assays

Source check: Source checked. Not independent scientific confirmation.

Finding: Eight stage/time-specific Bayesian classifiers trained on historical phenotypic measurements guided prospective selection of predicted active and inactive commercial compounds. In-vitro assays reported 48% and 34% hit fractions for somules and adults, followed by triage of five compounds. The selected-set fractions are not unbiased head-to-head screening rates; no animal cure, clinical mechanism, safety or efficacy is established.
